questions.q: Why can't you write WHERE COUNT(Id) > 10 in a SOQL query?
options: WHERE runs before grouping and filters individual rows, so filtering on an aggregate requires HAVING
COUNT is not a valid SOQL function
WHERE only accepts text comparisons
Aggregates are only allowed in ORDER BY
questions.explain: WHERE filters rows before aggregation. HAVING filters the groups after they are summarized.

questions.q: What is the correct clause order when a query uses WHERE, GROUP BY, HAVING, and ORDER BY?
options: WHERE, GROUP BY, HAVING, ORDER BY
GROUP BY, WHERE, HAVING, ORDER BY
HAVING, WHERE, GROUP BY, ORDER BY
WHERE, HAVING, GROUP BY, ORDER BY
questions.explain: Rows are filtered by WHERE, grouped by GROUP BY, groups are filtered by HAVING, then the results are sorted.

questions.q: A condition that does not involve an aggregate, such as Industry = 'Technology', should generally go where?
options: In WHERE, so it filters rows before grouping and leaves less work for the groups
In HAVING, because it is applied last
In ORDER BY
It does not matter, because both clauses are identical
questions.explain: Conditions that need no aggregate belong in WHERE. It is applied earlier, on individual rows.

questions.q: Which query finds Contact emails that appear on more than one record?
options: SELECT Email, COUNT(Id) FROM Contact GROUP BY Email HAVING COUNT(Id) > 1
SELECT Email FROM Contact WHERE COUNT(Id) > 1
SELECT Email, COUNT(Id) FROM Contact HAVING COUNT(Id) > 1 GROUP BY Email
SELECT DUPLICATE(Email) FROM Contact
questions.explain: Group by the field, count each group, and keep the groups with a count above one. GROUP BY comes before HAVING.

questions.q: In the duplicate-email query, why add WHERE Email != null?
options: Without it, all contacts with no email form one large null group with a meaningless count
SOQL cannot group by a field that has null values anywhere
It makes HAVING run faster because it is required syntax
It converts null emails to empty strings
questions.explain: Records with a null grouped field form their own group, which would dominate the duplicate results.
